series_label: Proportion of population using at least basic drinking water services
source_or_custodian: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (authoring entities: Richard Paul Johnston, WHO; Tom Slaymaker, UNICEF); the indicator metadata also lists World Development Indicators (World Bank) as a source. Database: Human Capital Project (WB_HCP).
release_or_vintage: Version 2, version date 2026-10-14. Time period 2000-2024 in the server metadata. Indicator metadata shows date_last_update and date_released as null.
status_or_notes: No 2025 observation was returned by the server, so 2025 is not included in values. The server's time period for this series is 2000-2024. The get_data call also reported a validation note that the member_economies_only ref_area filter was not applied; this does not affect the Nigeria values. Two related series exist on the server with the same concept: WB_WDI_SH_H2O_BASW_ZS (World Development Indicators, 2000-2024) and WB_CLEAR_JMP_DW_AB (CLEAR Water, 2000-2022, latest 2022). Values for those were not retrieved.
definition: Percentage of people using at least basic water services, including those using basic drinking water services and safely managed water services. Basic drinking water services are defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided the collection time is no more than 30 minutes for a round trip. Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.

query_or_url: data360_get_data(database_id=WB_HCP, indicator_id=WB_HCP_UNICEF_WATER, country_code=NGA, start_year=2000, end_year=2025); metadata via data360_get_metadata(database_id=WB_HCP, indicator_id=WB_HCP_UNICEF_WATER).
